article.headline: Second cold front brings wet and windy conditions across New Zealand
article.summary: MetService expects a second weather front to move up the South Island tomorrow, bringing rain and stronger winds.
article.body:
A maximum wind gust of 148km/h was recorded at Mt Kaukau at 5am during recent gales, signaling the severity of the weather systems hitting the country. While current conditions are beginning to ease, the arrival of a second front marks a distinct shift from the warm weekend weather.

This upcoming weather change is significant for residents as the front brings rain and stronger northwesterly winds across the South Island. For regions that have experienced dry conditions, such as the Canterbury High Country, this moisture provides a necessary shift in the local climate. However, the anticipated wind and rain will continue to impact travel and daily routines across the country.

According to MetService meteorologist Maddy Neal, the front will reach the lower South Island late tomorrow afternoon before progressing overnight into Thursday. Westland is expected to receive the heaviest rainfall, while Gore and Invercargill should prepare for stronger gusts. The lower North Island will likely see the front arrive by midday Thursday, with Wellington, Wairarapa, and Auckland experiencing showers throughout Wednesday and Thursday.

Temperatures are expected to turn noticeably cooler following last week's highs, which reached 29C in places like Hastings. While some sheltered areas on the North Island's east coast may remain warm on Wednesday and Thursday, overall temperatures will remain lower than previous records. Travelers are advised to monitor the situation, as the earlier storm forced the cancellation or diversion of about 40 flights at Wellington Airport and caused widespread power and road disruptions.

article.headline: India eyes series clinching victory as injury-hit New Zealand faces 2-0 deficit
article.summary: India aims to secure the five-match T20I series against New Zealand today in Wellington after establishing a 2-0 lead.
article.body:
New Zealand’s seam attack arrives in Wellington with significantly reduced firepower as bowlers Matt Henry and Lockie Ferguson sit out the third match of the series. The hosts are struggling for consistency, having claimed only four wickets across the first two fixtures in Christchurch. This lack of pressure has allowed India to remain comfortable, with the visitors currently leading 2-0 and eyeing a decisive series victory.

The conditions in Wellington could further favor the tourists, as the dew and late-day starts have historically made batting second a simpler task. New Zealand’s performance has been hampered by sloppy fielding, compounding the difficulty of overcoming a side that has remained unbeaten in bilateral series against the Blackcaps since the 2018/19 season. For the visiting Indian squad, this match serves as a golden opportunity to wrap up the series early.

Yahoo Sports reports that India enters the contest as the favorites with odds of 1.74, while New Zealand is priced at 2.06. The Blackcaps will look to debut a revised lineup featuring Finn Allen and Daryl Mitchell to counter India’s roster, which includes Shreyas Iyer and Arshdeep Singh. With the current series record standing at 2-0, India has the momentum to extend their dominance in New Zealand, where the bilateral series record between the two nations is currently deadlocked at 2-2.

Should India secure a win at Sky Stadium, they will add to their historical success in New Zealand, where they previously recorded a 5-0 sweep in 2019/20 and a 1-0 series win in 2022/23. New Zealand will need a quick turnaround to prevent the series from ending in the third match.

article.headline: Sri Lanka Routs Pakistan by Eight Wickets to Secure Tri-Series Final Spot
article.summary: Sri Lanka defeated Pakistan by eight wickets in Lahore on Tuesday, eliminating England from the tri-series final contention.
article.body:
Dilshan Madushanka dismantled the Pakistan batting lineup with a career-best 5-34, skittling the hosts for just 110 runs in 25.2 overs. Sri Lanka responded with clinical efficiency, reaching the modest target in only 18.1 overs to confirm their place in Saturday's final at the Gaddafi Stadium.

The result carries significant consequences for the tri-series structure, as it officially ends England's hopes of reaching the final. Harry Brook's side, which sits at three defeats from three matches, was eliminated from the tournament entirely due to this outcome. Thursday's upcoming fixture between Sri Lanka and England is now rendered a dead rubber, as the finalists are already determined.

Pakistan captain Babar Azam provided the top score for his team with 29 runs, though the hosts struggled to build any meaningful partnerships throughout the innings. In reply, Sri Lanka's Kamindu Mendis anchored the chase with an unbeaten 62 off 60 balls. Mendis survived an early dropped catch and a successful lbw review at 44 to guide his team to victory, striking eight fours and two sixes in the process. According to The Guardian, Sri Lanka finished the match with more than 31 overs to spare.

Sri Lanka will now prepare for the championship decider against Pakistan on Saturday. Before that showpiece event, the tournament schedule continues with the remaining group match on Thursday, marking the end of England's involvement in the series before they travel to Australia for their next tour.

article.headline: Alexandra Eala Routs Mika Stojsavljevic in Tokyo to Reach Second Round
article.summary: Alexandra Eala advanced at the Toray Pan Pacific Open after defeating Mika Stojsavljevic 6-1, 6-2 on Monday.
article.body:
Alexandra Eala needed only 75 minutes to dismantle 17-year-old wild card Mika Stojsavljevic, surrendering just three games in a dominant 6-1, 6-2 victory. While Stojsavljevic managed to fire off 24 winners compared to Eala's eight, the 21-year-old Filipina maintained control by forcing the Briton into 41 unforced errors. Eala’s composure was most evident when she faced a 0-40 deficit early in the second set, recovering immediately with two service winners to hold her serve. This victory for the 2022 US Open junior champion effectively halted the momentum of her younger opponent, who was making her main-draw debut at the event.

The clinical performance highlights Eala’s maturation on the professional circuit as she navigates the Tokyo field. By keeping her error count low and landing 68% of her first serves, Eala demonstrated the tactical discipline required to sustain deep tournament runs, setting a strong pace as competition intensifies.

According to the WTA, Eala’s serve remained a key asset, winning 72% of points on her first delivery. The match saw a contrast in styles between the consistent ball-striking of the No. 8 seed and the high-risk, high-reward approach of the World No. 411. The tournament also saw significant shifts in the draw, as No. 2 seed Maja Chwalinska withdrew with a left thigh injury and defending champion Belinda Bencic pulled out due to a right ankle issue.

Eala will face Talia Gibson in the second round. Gibson earned her spot after securing a 6-0, 7-5 victory over Daria Kasatkina in an all-Australian clash. This next match represents a critical test for Eala, as Gibson carries the momentum of a hot start, having won the first eight games of her previous match.

article.headline: South Africa and Australia clash at Newlands in final Test series decider
article.summary: South Africa and Australia meet in the third Test at Newlands starting October 27 with the series level at 1-1.
article.body:
South Africa enters the series finale following a commanding innings and 31-run victory in Gqeberha, a match where they remarkably forced Australia to lose 13 wickets in a single day. The Proteas secured that win despite a morning session washout and the loss of frontline bowler Anrich Nortje to a groin injury during his fourth over. Australia, meanwhile, looks to regain momentum after suffering a 214-run defeat in the second Test, having previously dominated the series opener in Durban. With the series tied, the final Test serves as a direct showdown to determine the winner of the contest.

This match carries significant weight for both squads, as the outcome will settle a hard-fought series that has seen both teams secure decisive wins. For the hosts, the challenge lies in replacing the injured Nortje, with Gerald Coetzee, Corbin Bosch, Dane Paterson, and Keshav Maharaj listed as potential options to bolster the attack. Australia faces its own personnel questions, including a late fitness test for Steve Smith regarding a neck issue and a decision on whether to rotate between bowler Nathan Lyon and Scott Boland.

article.summary: Host Alfonso Ribeiro rejected allegations that show eliminations are fixed after former contestants suggested producers influence final results.
article.body:
During the October 22 episode of the LexLos podcast, former contestant Alexa PenaVega recounted a conversation from season 21 with fellow competitor Hayes Grier. Grier, who commanded millions of social media followers, reportedly felt the show was rigged after landing in the bottom three. Alexa noted that while she believes viewer votes and judge scores matter, the program is also heavily produced to follow a specific narrative. She pointed to season 21 winner Bindi Irwin, suggesting producers maintained her presence on the show because of her compelling story. Further, Alexa and Carlos PenaVega claimed that production often knows who will be eliminated before the live broadcast because travel arrangements for press appearances on programs like The View must be finalized in advance. According to Alexa, her professional partner, Mark Ballas, was notified of their impending elimination through such industry connections before it was announced on air.

The discussion highlights ongoing tensions regarding transparency in reality competition formats. For viewers, these claims question the weight of public participation versus behind-the-scenes decision-making in determining which celebrities advance. The debate is not limited to season 21; season 18 contestant Sean Avery previously claimed his early exit was fueled by personal disagreements with a producer rather than his standing in the competition.

Host and season 19 winner Alfonso Ribeiro pushed back against these assertions when the podcast clip surfaced on social media. Ribeiro dismissed the rigging claims as inaccurate, stating that keeping popular contestants in the competition is basic logic for the show's success. Alexa later clarified that the social media clips of her podcast appearance were taken out of context, noting that her intention was to tell a story about Grier's perspective rather than present a formal accusation.

Maplin reported that torch sales nearly quadrupled within three days, while major online grocer Ocado saw specific brands of bottled water and soup ranges sell out completely following the government’s "be ready" announcement. Managing director at Maplin, Ollie Marshall, noted that consumers are acting on advice to secure affordable products that maintain household connectivity during power outages.

This trend follows a call from Defence Secretary Wes Streeting for citizens to store three litres of water per person daily, along with baby food and non-perishable items. The initiative aims to improve national resilience against threats such as cyber attacks or extreme weather events, including recent disruption caused by storms. While supermarkets like Iceland maintain healthy supply levels, other chains continue to work with partners to restock daily as demand remains high.

The surge in preparedness activity comes amid reports of vulnerabilities in web architecture and concerns regarding the security of undersea cable networks. Defence Secretary Streeting praised the public for taking practical steps to manage potential disruptions from incidents like burst pipes or flooding. As stores manage intermittent shortages, officials urge the public to continue checking for replenished inventory as they build their three-day survival kits.

article.headline: Winless Nets Storm TD Garden Seeking Upset Against Reigning Atlantic Division Champions
article.summary: The Boston Celtics host the Brooklyn Nets at 7:30 p.m. ET as the home team looks to keep the visitors winless on the season.
article.body:
The Brooklyn Nets arrive at TD Garden in search of their first victory, currently carrying the league's fifth-worst net rating with an average margin of 11.8 points lost per 100 possessions. Brooklyn enters the matchup with an 0-3 record, reeling from a 136-109 defeat to the Indiana Pacers. Head coach Jordi Fernandez described the team's performance following the first quarter against Indiana as unacceptable, noting that surrendering 112 points over three quarters makes winning nearly impossible.

For the Celtics, the game serves as a test on the second night of a back-to-back following a 134-99 win over the Chicago Bulls. While Boston’s Jayson Tatum leads the team with averages of 24 points and eight assists, the status of starters Paul George and Mitchell Robinson remains a situational decision for head coach Joe Mazzulla. Given their limited minutes during Monday’s blowout victory, the pair may see action against a Brooklyn squad led by Julius Randle, who currently averages 22 points, seven rebounds, and 6.3 assists per game.

Boston enters the contest as a 12.5-point favorite with an over/under set at 222.5 points. The SportsLine Projection Model, which has simulated the matchup 10,000 times, is currently favoring the Under, projecting a combined 219 points as the total falls short of the line 57% of the time. This clash marks the first meeting of the season between the two Atlantic Division teams.

Following tonight's action, the Celtics maintain a brief two-day break before returning to the court on Friday for a rematch against the Bulls.

article.headline: Mitchell Starc Claims Six-for as Australia Dismisses South Africa for 329
article.summary: Mitchell Starc took six wickets on day one of the third Test as Australia bowled out South Africa for 329 in Cape Town.
article.body:
Mitchell Starc spearheaded the Australian bowling effort on the opening day at Newlands, claiming six wickets to curb South Africa’s momentum. The visitors successfully dismissed the hosts for a total of 329 after a testing start to the series decider. Australia, who entered the match following a series-leveling loss in the second Test, faced early difficulties as their bowling unit attempted to navigate a flat surface in Cape Town.

The performance of the pace attack proved vital as the series currently sits at 1-1. Following a difficult morning session that drew comparisons to Australia's 2005 experience at Edgbaston, the team relied on Starc’s precision to prevent South Africa from building an even larger first-innings total. This match marks a critical juncture for the tourists, who entered the game having made four changes to their starting XI.

Selection drama surrounded the match, with Steve Smith ruled out shortly before play due to a neck injury, while Scott Boland was omitted despite his strong career record. Cooper Connolly, aged 23, joined the side for his second Test appearance as the team sought to address recent struggles. The crowd at Newlands, the site of the 2018 series controversy, remained a vocal presence throughout the day's play.

Australia’s bowling dominance provided a necessary shift in the contest as they look to regain control of the decider. With the South African innings closed at 329, the focus now shifts to the Australian top order to stabilize the game and respond to the target set by the hosts.

article.headline: Shorthanded Kings face grim odds as defending champions Spurs host Tuesday tilt
article.summary: The winless Sacramento Kings travel to face the San Antonio Spurs this Tuesday while struggling with four key players ruled out due to injury.
article.body:
The Sacramento Kings enter Tuesday's matchup against the San Antonio Spurs riding a three-game losing streak that has left them ranking last in the league for blocks, assists, and Player Impact Estimate. While the Kings search for their first victory of the 2026-27 season, they must contend with the defending Western Conference champions who are simultaneously looking to climb back to a .500 record after opening their own campaign with one win in three outings.

For the Kings, the challenge is compounded by a significant injury report that has sidelined four players. The team confirmed that starting forward Keegan Murray will remain out for two weeks, while backup centers Dylan Cardwell and Maxime Raynaud are unavailable for the next week to 14 days. Veteran Ben Simmons also remains out for the duration of the season following Achilles tendon repair surgery. These absences force the Kings to rely heavily on role players like Precious Achiuwa and Jonathan Mogbo to fill the void, as the team attempts to improve a defense that has conceded over 120 points in each of their three previous contests.

According to Yahoo Sports, the Spurs maintain a clear advantage heading into the contest, as they deal with fewer health concerns than their opponents. Pounding The Rock notes that the Sacramento backcourt faces a thin roster of available guard talent, increasing the pressure on established scorers like De’Andre Hunter and Malik Monk to dictate the pace. Both teams are looking to secure a win on the first leg of San Antonio’s second back-to-back series of the season.

The game serves as a critical junction for the Kings, who have struggled to replicate their previous postseason form, while the Spurs aim to capitalize on the matchup to find momentum.

news.og_title: Shelton on Sinner and Alcaraz's season: "It's sad for tennis"
news.og_desc: Ben Shelton is ready to assert his authority in a truly challenging ATP 500 Basel 2026, where he is the top seed. The American is guaranteed his spot at the ATP Finals, but he wants to take advantage of this situation to play with less pressure and showcase his best tennis ahead of the Masters tournament, which is his top priority for the rest of the year.In his press conference before the tournament starts, Shelton was asked whether he believes the dominance of Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz is coming to an end due to the rise of other players, like himself, this season and the injuries that have affected the Italian and the Spaniard. His response was unequivocal.Shelton is emphatic regarding Sinner and Alcaraz"They have won two of the four Grand Slams held this year and Sinner has secured five Masters 1000 titles. I don’t know to what extent it can be said that their dominance has diminished.""I believe both will probably come in very good condition for next year's Australian Open. It has been unfortunate for tennis that they have not been able to compete for part of this season.""But, honestly, I wouldn't go so far as to say that their dominance is fading. It is true that there are more young players competing for the major titles and gaining prominence, but to say they are losing their supremacy seems unfair to me."These words from Ben Shelton clearly demonstrate the great respect that all tennis players have for both Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz, and that strong feeling that when both are in form, they remain at a higher level than the rest. It will be interesting to see if the American can continue to close that gap in the coming times.
